summary: Ben Joffe works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder, studying under doctoral supervisor Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London (~2008-2013) and held teaching posts at the University of Virginia (~2014-2017) and the University of Bristol (~2017).

Benimadhab Barua (1888-1948) was an Indian scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Chittagong College, Krishnagar Government College, Krishnath College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of London, he held a post at Calcutta from 1918 to 1948.

Benjamin A. Elman is a scholar of Sinology and history. Educated at Hamilton College, American University, and the University of Pennsylvania, he served as Professor of Chinese History at UCLA (attested 2004) and directed Princeton's East Asian Studies Program (~2005-2012).
Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., also studying with Janet Gyatso and Gareth Sparham.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford (~2004-2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2010-2016).

Benjamin Wood specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thupten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio (1876-1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1902-1905). He held posts at Waseda University, Taisho University (~1926-1943), and served as head of Sanko Library (~1947-1968).

Benoît Vermander works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied at Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Facultés Loyola Paris. He served as Academic Director of Taipei Ricci Institute (1996-2009) and joined Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, having studied at Paris Diderot and the University of Paris. He held academic posts at Cornell (~1983-1987), Stanford (~1987-2006), and Columbia University (~2006).

Bernard Frank (1927-1996) was a specialist in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He headed the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972-1977) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979-1996).

Bernhard Geiger (1881-1964) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1899-1904), he held posts there (~1909-1938), at the Tibetan-Iranian Institute (1938-1951), and at Columbia University (~1947-1951).
Bernhard Hirzel (1807-1847) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Franz Bopp (~1830-1833). He later served as a Dozent at the University of Zurich (~1833-1839).

Bernhard Kölver (1938-2001) was an Indologist who held posts at the University of Cologne (1966-1970), the Nepal Research Centre (~1970-1972), the University of Kiel as professor (1977-1993), and Leipzig University (1993-2001).

Bernie Glassman (1939-2018) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at NYU Tandon School of Engineering (~1956-1960), he studied under Taizan Maezumi (~1967-1995) and founded Zen Peacemakers (attested 2002).

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Leiden University and Oxford, she earned her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk (~2009-2015) and held posts at Heidelberg University (~2014-2016) and Leiden University (2015-2016).

Berthold Delbrück (1842-1922) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott and Albrecht Weber. He held a post at Halle-Wittenberg (1867) and the Sanskrit chair at the University of Jena (1870-1913).

Berthold Laufer (1874-1934) studied Sinology, Tibetology, and Central Asian studies at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1904-1908) and the Field Museum of Natural History (~1908-1934).

Bettina Bäumer is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Salzburg who studied under Lakshman Joo. She has held posts at the Alice Boner Institute, Abhinavagupta Research Library, IIAS, and the University of Vienna.
Bettine Birge works in Sinology and history. She completed her PhD at Columbia University, studying under William Theodore de Bary, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.
